To collect sound from the air

Why is hearing loss caused by loud noise usually permanent?

questions.prompt: A sound level increases from 60 dB to 80 dB. Roughly how many times more intense is it?
questions.explain: Each 10 dB is 10 times the intensity: 10 × 10 = 100.

questions.prompt: Match each part of the ear to its job.
questions.explain: Each part passes the sound energy on in a different form.

questions.prompt: Many teenagers listen to music through earphones for hours at high volume. Explain the risk and suggest two sensible rules.
questions.modelAnswer: High volume for long periods (above about 85 dB) over-stimulates and damages the hair cells in the cochlea. These cells do not grow back, so the hearing loss is permanent and often gradual and painless. Sensible rules: keep the volume at or below about 60% and take a break after about 60 minutes; use noise-cancelling headphones so you don’t need to turn the volume up in noisy places.
rubric: Loud sound damages cochlea hair cells
Two practical rules (volume limit, time limit, breaks, noise-cancelling)
